observation.visible_scene: A wide beach view at sunset (or sunrise): a layered sky of orange, gold and teal clouds sits above a flat ocean horizon with a bright sun glow near center-right. A band of breaking surf runs horizontally across the middle of the frame, and the foreground is wet, mirror-like sand that reflects the orange and blue of the sky. The composition, cloud shapes, horizon height and sun position stay essentially unchanged throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: The surf zone shows continuous, low-amplitude wave motion: the white foam line and crest texture shift position and shape from frame to frame, indicating small waves rolling toward and across the shore rather than a single fixed edge.
The thin sheet of water and the ripples on the wet sand shimmer and reorganize, so the bright reflection patches in the foreground subtly change brightness and outline as the water moves.
The sky, cloud formations and horizon glow remain effectively static over the ~2.7 s window (no visible cloud drift or sun movement at this timescale).
The framing is stable: the horizon line and cloud features hold the same pixel positions, consistent with a stationary camera rather than a pan or zoom.
outside_clip_unknowns: The longer-term evolution of the sunset, the tide level, and whether the wave pattern is part of a larger swell cycle are not shown.
Any motion before t=0 or after t=2.669 s is unknown; the segment is an arbitrary crop of continuous footage.
uncertain_details: The exact number and direction of individual wave crests is hard to disambiguate because the foam and reflection changes are small and partly overlap.
The orange/teal shapes in the foreground are reflections on wet sand, not separate physical objects, but the precise water depth under them cannot be confirmed.
Residual camera motion (very slight drift) cannot be fully ruled out, though background evidence suggests the camera is essentially fixed.
